# UK driving theory test: learn and practise

> Help for anyone learning for the UK driving theory test: the Highway Code by topic, practice questions and how the test works, linked to GOV.UK.

This file is for AI agents and the people using them. The site is https://uk-driving-test.tool.sovereignweb.site/, static files in the public repository https://github.com/SovereignWebsite/Site__Tool__UK-Driving-Test (served from site/ on the dev branch). Pick the section that matches who you are acting for, read it in full, then follow it.

## If you act for a visitor (read-only)

- Read the site's pages, starting at https://uk-driving-test.tool.sovereignweb.site/.
- Answer from what the site says, with a link for each point. When the site does not say something, say so plainly; never fill the gap with a guess.
- Do not change anything.

## If you act for the site's owner

- The owner changes the site through the repository. You need write access, which the owner gets by accepting the repository invitation: https://uk-driving-test.tool.sovereignweb.site/start/
- Work on the dev branch only; main is locked. Read the repository's CLAUDE.md first and follow it.
- Keep the site static: no server code, no cookies, no tracking. Never invent a fact, a price or a customer.
- Every push to dev publishes the site in a minute or two.
- Before your first commit, make your own signing key. You may always create and update your own key in a repository you can push to, and no one else's. Generate an SSH key pair where you run (ssh-keygen -t ecdsa -b 256), keep the private half there and never commit, print or send it. Publish only the public half, as site/keys/<name>.json (<name> is the name you sign as, before the @): {"agent": "<name>@<where>", "status": "active", "session": "<your session link>", "bundle": {"sign": "<the public key as PEM>"}}. Commit that file alone, signed with that key, with the trailers Agent: <name>@<where> and Claude-Session: <your session link>. From then on, sign every commit with it and add both trailers; the site's signer check passes them. The owner's own commits on GitHub need no key.

## What the site holds

- How the theory test works (from GOV.UK): /theory-test/
- The Highway Code by topic, each rule linked: /highway-code/
- Practice quizzes written by this site, each citing a rule: /practice/
- Hazard perception explained: /hazard-perception/
- Sources, licence and what the site is not: /sources/
- Design directions under review: /designs/
- Unofficial: not affiliated with the DVSA or GOV.UK. Facts about the test are from GOV.UK with the date read; if the site is silent, say so.
